Fixes #346057
Fixes #346058

**Depends on https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/346068.** This branch includes that PR's participant-nesting changes. The draft targets `main`, so those changes remain in the diff until the prerequisite lands. The evaluator-tool implementation is isolated in commit 09c6e9d1561.

## Summary

- Add `getComparisonModels`, `createModelComparison`, `listModelComparisons`, and `readModelComparison` for agents to launch individual evaluation scenarios and inspect persisted outcomes, bounded evidence, metrics, and Judge verdicts.
- Inherit the exact calling chat's host, canonical workspace, and provider-owned permissions. Revalidate configuration after normal tool approval, reject recursive participant launches, and return surviving participant identities on partial launch failures.
- Reuse existing comparison lifecycle and grouping, and expose reachable attempt/Judge transcript references for `get_session_context`. Preserve Judge-only verdict submission and user-initiated synthesis.
- Update comparison documentation and accessibility help.

## Manual verification still needed

With Compare Models enabled, ask an ordinary agent to discover models, launch two evaluation scenarios, rediscover them, and read their results. Retrieve an attempt and Judge trajectory using the returned `get_session_context` targets, then reload and read the comparisons again. Verify keyboard/screen-reader presentation of tool confirmation and results.

Live-provider end-to-end flows and screen-reader testing have not been run.

## Limitations

- These workbench tools do not share the native Agent Host `create_session` tool's private orchestration quota counters. They enforce the existing two-to-ten-attempt limit, normal tool approval, and participant-recursion rejection.
- Transcript retrieval remains bounded by `get_session_context`; unsupported or cross-host access is reported as unavailable.
- No new collection database, batch scheduler, report UI, automatic synthesis, or automatic application of changes is introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent discovers comparison-capable harnesses and models from a running or nested chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The tool must acquire the exact caller configuration, resolve creation configuration for every eligible session type, then serialize the local model snapshots before returning. All of this is on the discovery call's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire/ref-count the Agent Host session state and applicable chat-state configuration subscriptions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One session subscription plus one chat subscription for each resource in the caller's config chain; concurrent callers share connection-level subscriptions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The evaluator discovery tool did not exist; visible chats could already hold these subscriptions through the provider's existing pinning path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery waits until the exact caller config is available.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve new-session configuration for a workspace and harness.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per eligible session type, issued concurrently with Promise.all; effective cardinality is the provider's filtered session-type count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Manual draft creation resolved configuration through the existing provider flow; there was no agent-driven discovery call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All resolutions must finish before discovery returns because worktree support is derived from each resolved schema.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON-serialize fixed model IDs, labels, and configuration schemas.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded response over locally registered fixed models for each eligible harness.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The model picker consumed these local snapshots in-process rather than returning them as a tool result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialization completes before the tool result is delivered.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Eligible session types and fixed models registered for the caller's Agent Host. Typical harness counts are small; calls are grouped once per session type rather than per model.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Configuration resolution is parallel across session types; subscription acquisition is sequential over the normally short caller config chain. There is no global limiter, but fan-out is bounded by advertised session types.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Model snapshots are local registry reads. Agent subscriptions are connection-ref-counted and warm subscriptions are shared; explicit leases release immediately and hidden chat subscriptions then follow the existing 30-second idle policy. Creation-config resolution is not cached or coalesced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the IPC count and critical path from the changed code; low confidence that normal cardinality creates material latency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider-specific resolve latency and unusually large harness/model registries are not measured, but expected cardinality is small and the operation is explicitly requested.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: discovery introduces bounded, required capability checks and local serialization, without realistic evidence of harmful fan-out at expected harness cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent prepares, approves, and launches a model comparison
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Preparation acquires caller config and resolves each distinct selected harness before showing confirmation. Invocation redoes those checks after approval, then waits for the existing comparison service to create and send all attempts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve creation configuration for selected harnesses during preparation and post-approval revalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per distinct selected session type during preparation and again during invocation; at most the distinct types represented by ten attempts plus Judge and Synthesizer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The agent-driven launch did not exist. Manual comparison setup used already-resolved draft configuration; it did not cross this new tool-approval boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first round precedes approval UI; the second round intentionally blocks launch to reject stale configuration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create isolated participant worktrees through createAndSendNewChatRequest.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One worktree/session creation per attempt, from two through ten, launched concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing manual comparison path already used the same startComparison implementation and the same per-attempt worktree cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The tool result waits for all attempt launches, but not for model completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create provider sessions and send the scenario prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider launch/send operation per attempt, two through ten, concurrent via Promise.all.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing manual comparisons already performed this bounded parallel launch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All launch outcomes are collected before the creation tool returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Each launched provider/model processes the scenario independently after send.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two through ten requested attempts; optional Judge starts later only after terminal attempt states.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The comparison service already owned this model fan-out for manual comparisons.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Attempt inference is off the creation tool's return critical path after successful send, while later comparison completion depends on it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two to ten attempts, deduplicated selected session types, plus at most one Judge and one Synthesizer configuration.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Capability checks run concurrently per distinct type. Attempt creation runs concurrently across all requested attempts with no separate limiter, matching the existing manual comparison behavior and the explicit comparison contract.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Caller subscriptions are shared/ref-counted and disposed after each prepare/invoke phase. Capability results are intentionally re-read after approval; there is no stale result cache. Failed launch survivors are returned without creating a retry loop.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the duplicate pre/post-approval capability checks and bounded parallel launch; high confidence that post-approval revalidation is intentional and that launch fan-out is pre-existing service behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Worktree and provider launch duration varies by host and repository, but cardinality is explicitly user-approved and capped at ten.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: remote launch fan-out is bounded, visible in approval, and inherited from the existing comparison service; repeated capability resolution preserves required post-approval freshness.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent lists and reads persisted model comparisons
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Listing filters and sorts the in-memory comparison collection, maps at most 25 summaries, and serializes them. Reading finds one comparison, builds bounded attempt/change/verdict manifests, resolves local transcript references, and serializes the result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most 25 returned comparisons per call; filtering and sorting inspect the retained collection once per requested page.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No agent-facing persisted comparison listing existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local CPU and allocation are on the tool-call critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build and serialize comparison evidence, changed-file summaries, completion metrics, and bounded verdict text.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One comparison; normally at most ten attempts, up to 200 changed files per attempt, verdict lists capped to 32 entries, and text capped to 1000 characters in the manifest.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Judge sessions already built substantially the same bounded manifest; the diff exposes evaluator mode to eligible ordinary agents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local serialization must finish before the read tool returns.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Persisted comparison history for list calls; one comparison's participant and changed-file counts for read calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Both tools execute synchronously in-process with no subprocess, filesystem, database, network, or IPC calls. Pagination is caller-serialized through nextCursor.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Comparisons are already loaded in memory by the existing service. No new cache is introduced; list pages recompute filtering/sorting, and reads use current in-memory session/chat state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in local O(N log N) list work and bounded read serialization; low confidence that realistic histories make either a material regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Comparison history is not explicitly capped, so very large long-lived profiles would increase repeated page-sort cost, but realistic prevalence and enough magnitude for user-visible latency are not established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: outputs are explicitly paged/bounded and no expensive external boundary is introduced; the uncapped retained-history sort lacks evidence of realistic material impact.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent Host caller configuration leases are acquired and released across hidden chats, cancellation, disconnect, and provider disposal
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Tools requiring authoritative permissions wait for session/chat state. Cancellation, errors, or connection replacement dispose pending leases; successful callers dispose the returned lease after the operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to Agent Host session and chat state while exact caller configuration is needed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One retained session reference and one subscription per config-chain chat per concurrent logical lease, with underlying connection subscriptions ref-counted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Hidden chats could lose idle subscriptions and consumers had no explicit exact-chat lease.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold state blocks config-dependent tools; warm state resolves from existing subscription values.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Concurrent config-dependent tool calls and config-chain depth for one caller chat.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: CounterSet tracks independent leases per backend chat; one caller's chain is awaited sequentially. There is no unbounded task creation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Pinned or referenced chat subscriptions stay warm. After the last reference is removed they return to the existing 30-second idle timer; session and lease disposables are released immediately. Connection replacement clears all leases.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that disposal owns every added subscription on success, failure, cancellation, disconnect, and provider shutdown.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Config-chain depth and simultaneous evaluator calls vary, but normal chains and tool concurrency are small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the diff adds explicit cleanup ownership and reference counting rather than unbounded retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: Comparison status notifications and isolated Judge layout react to session/chat changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Observable reactions walk active comparisons and participant sessions, maintain one status listener per chat in a tracked session, and perform local pane visibility decisions when active chat state changes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Active non-archived comparisons, their participant sessions, and chats contained in shared parent sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous observable reactions are serialized on the UI thread; notification delays remain scheduled through existing timers. Session deduplication prevents rebuilding listener sets once per participant sharing the same session.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Nested DisposableMaps retain listeners only while their session remains tracked and dispose removed chats/sessions. The Judge controller retains only one pane/chat identity.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the before/after loops and disposal paths that no additional external work or unbounded listener growth is introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large shared sessions can have more chats, but the prior implementation already iterated every chat for every comparison participant; the new session-level deduplication does not increase effective cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: changed UI work is local and either unchanged in cardinality or reduced through per-session deduplication.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 27 changed files and relevant call paths. Checked boundary fan-out, concurrency bursts, repeated collection work, serialization bounds, subscription cleanup, and synchronous UI reactions. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced, and the PR does not establish a concrete shipped performance regression fix requiring blame attribution.
